findings.where: Phone, first screen: the section drawing above the name block
findings.fault: At 390 px the drawing shrinks to a thin strip about 130 px tall, roughly a sixth of the first screen. The name, the role lines, the lede and the button fill the rest. On the phone the words lead and the picture is a header ornament, which reverses the direction's 'the picture leads and the words wait'.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for one calm picture or moment before any text asks for anything, and many of whose bank and agency visitors will first open the link on a phone. They get a text page with a small drawing on top, not the calm sheet that desktop gets.

findings.where: Phone, the texture tile (earth hatch and poche swatches in their framed box)
findings.fault: On desktop the box has inner padding and a dimension line under the swatches. At 390 px the padding is gone: the 'EARTH HATCH' label and the hatch swatch sit flush on the box's left edge, and the poche swatch runs flush to its right edge. The dimension line is reduced to an empty bordered strip under the swatches. The tile looks broken and cropped instead of drawn.
findings.who_objects: Mark and Angélique, reviewing the tile on a phone to judge this look. It reads as a layout bug and makes the blueprint direction look less finished than it is.

findings.where: Desktop, first screen: the title-block nav row (DRAWING MMM-GA-001 and SCALE NTS cells beside PROFILE, ARTICLES, BLOG, CONTACT)
findings.fault: Similarity and common region: the two static drawing-data cells sit in the same row as the four links, with the same divided cells, the same light caps and the same height. The row reads as six menu items, two of which do nothing. On the phone they move to the logo row and the problem goes away.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the menu, who may click 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page, or spend a moment working out which cells are navigation.

findings.where: Desktop, first screen: the right end of the ground line in the section drawing
findings.fault: Continuity and figure/ground: past the last arch, the ground line runs on and turns up into a lone thin curve that ends near the sheet's right border. It sits outside both dimension chains and is not tied to anything in the drawing. It reads as a stray stroke and pulls the composition off-centre toward the frame edge.
findings.who_objects: An engineer or development-bank reader used to real section drawings, for whom an unexplained line on a general arrangement looks careless. That works against a look built on 'measured, exact'.

findings.where: Desktop, the article specimen and motion sketch row (bottom of the sheet)
findings.fault: The article column ends about 220 px above the motion-sketch box beside it, so the two-column row closes on a lopsided empty hole at the bottom left of the sheet.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reading the tile as the finished look of his site, where an uneven, unfinished-looking bottom edge undercuts the precise drawing-sheet conceit.

findings.where: Phone, first screen: the role lines under the name ('LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A •' / 'SCALE NTS')
findings.fault: The line breaks right after the bullet. The separator is left hanging at the end of one line and 'SCALE NTS' drops to the next, so the small caption block looks ragged under the clean rule.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader on a phone, who sees a stray dot. It's minor, but it's in the most-seen block of the page.
